subject: Potential FinSight telemetry anomaly — request for IR runbook and evidence transfer
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice@finsight.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Unusual token spike — preliminary notify

Jonas / Marissa,

We observed an unusual burst of embeddings requests originating from our tenant between 08:42 and 08:46 PST this morning. Volume is roughly 12x our baseline and some request payloads look like batched exports. We do not yet have evidence of customer data exfiltration but wanted to notify your security team immediately and request the following:

1) Redwood IR runbook (latest) and contact for escalation (pager or phone).
2) Any sampled telemetry and request logs that correspond to the window 2026-12-19T08:40:00-08:50:00 PST (redacted where necessary).
3) Expected timeline for an initial triage update.

Attached is a small log excerpt we pulled on our side that shows request hashes and timestamps: finsight_alert_log_excerpt.tar.gz [attachment: finsight_alert_log_excerpt.tar.gz (text/tar)].

Please confirm receipt and next steps.

Thanks,
Alice Park
Head of Security Operations, FinSight Inc.
alice@finsight.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@finsight.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unusual token spike — preliminary notify

Alice — thanks for the heads up and the excerpt. We are marking this as an incident and will begin triage now. Immediate notes / asks: 

- Karthik (SecOps) is on this thread and will pull server-side request/ingest logs and rate-limiter telemetry for the window you specified.
- Marissa (Customer Security Liaison) will coordinate with your SOC on evidence transfer and data redaction needs.
- Can you confirm whether those batched payloads contained PII or were internal test data? Any sample IDs help.

We will provide an initial status update within 90 minutes and share a temporary evidence drop location for log artifacts. Also attaching our current IR runbook (v3.2) for your reference: redwood_ir_runbook_v3.2.pdf [attachment: redwood_ir_runbook_v3.2.pdf].

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Park <alice@finsight.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unusual token spike — preliminary notify

Quick triage update (internal notes included inline):

- Confirmed a burst from an API key associated with FinSight (key id redacted). Peak qps ~ 11.8x baseline at 08:44 PST.
- No successful privilege escalation events observed in the IAM logs.
- We pulled request/response digests and sampled payloads for 08:40–08:50 and uploaded sanitized artifacts to the shared evidence folder: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/IR-FinSight-2026-12-21 (link for FinSight SOC only).

Internal action items (for the postmortem and compliance mapping):
- Preserve full tenant audit trail for 90 days (retention override in place).
- Run quick compare of embeddings outputs against known corpora to detect exfil patterns.
- Prepare SIG/SOC2 evidence slice: sampling matrix, redaction rubric, and extraction commands used.

I'll deliver an internal initial findings summary in two hours and then a customer-friendly one in three.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@finsight.com>, Tom Delgado <tom.delgado@finsight.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 14:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Postmortem and evidence transfer — FinSight incident (IR-7894)

Alice and Tom —

Thanks for bearing with us while we completed the triage and root cause analysis. Summary and deliverables below: 

Summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: Misconfigured client-side automation in a FinSight pipeline sent batched requests using a long-lived API key during a maintenance job; not the result of a Redwood platform compromise.
- Scope: 11.8x request spike observed; sampled payloads contained internal test vectors and no confirmed customer PII.
- Impact: No cross-tenant data leakage or unauthorized account access detected.

Deliverables: 
- Full sanitized postmortem PDF: redwood_ir_postmortem_20261221.pdf [attachment: redwood_ir_postmortem_20261221.pdf] (includes timeline, root cause analysis, remediation steps, and SIG/SOC2 evidence crosswalk).
- Evidence folder (telemetry + sampling manifest): https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/IR-FinSight-2026-12-21
- JIRA ticket for tracking follow-ups: JIRA-IR-7894

Recommended next steps for FinSight: 
- Rotate the affected API key and confirm replacement with scoped short-lived keys.
- Add request rate guards on the maintenance job to prevent large-scale batching.
- If you need an attestation letter for SOC 2 evidence, Marissa will coordinate the statements we can provide and the scope.

Please confirm receipt and let us know if you want a 30-minute walkthrough with our SecOps and SREs — happy to schedule.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
[Redwood Inference]
